focus.jnote: The worst of last week's shock has settled, but the tape is still fragile. The S&P 500 gained 0.32% to 7,376.86, the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.1% to 24,579.43, while the Dow slipped 0.46% to 51,285.73. The recovery was led by technology: the semiconductor index jumped 4.2%, with Nvidia +2.8% and AMD +11%. But the damage was real — the Nasdaq lost 3.37% on the week, the S&P fell 2.68% (its largest weekly decline since the week ended April 4, 2025), and the Dow declined 0.94%. Volatility came in but stayed high: the one-day gauge fell ~22% to 28.73 and the VIX fell ~9% to 25.64, while the regime remains high-volatility bear, the curve in backwardation and SKEW elevated at 153.55. Monday futures are firmer — S&P 500 futures +0.47%, Nasdaq 100 futures +0.33%, Dow futures +0.71%. The big overhang is data: October payrolls came in at +165K against roughly 60K expected and unemployment fell to 4.1%, markets price around a 78% chance of a December hike, and US CPI follows on Tuesday.
focus.notdown: Of the boarded names, none is a clean bullish Sniper today. The one defensive-ish structural fit is the MMM breakout, but it carries a negative gap this morning (see setups). The two Type A names are tagged bearish by the scanner — and critically, the live data contradicts both biases: Akamai's Q3 beat (EPS +5.85%, revenue +0.37%) and the stock rose +6.74% Friday, and IREN's AI cloud scaled hard, with AI cloud revenue reaching $200 million of $228 million total, and the stock jumped ~20%. On a VIX-26, backwardated tape with CPI tomorrow, every one is watch-only — and the honest answer is to sell nothing new.
focus.notup: The bearish Type A gaps (AKAM, IREN) are the scanner's picks, but the realized moves went the OTHER way — both gapped UP on beats, not down on misses. Selling a bear call into a name that just rallied on strong results is the opposite of a Sniper edge, and doing it on a VIX-26 rebound tape with CPI pending invites a violent squeeze. The disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today and let the scanner's conflicting fundamentals be verified first.
focus.why: Why RED? Two independent locks: P(≥1% gap) at ~44% is well above the 35% trigger, and CPI lands Tuesday at 8:30 ET — a Fed-watched print that forbids GREEN on its own. On top of that, the VIX is still ~25.6 with the curve in backwardation and SKEW elevated, the hallmark of an unstable, headline-whippy tape. Stand down on new credit spreads, or if you must be positioned, push DTE past the CPI print and the vol spike and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.
